newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-NORMAN WINS AUSTRALIAN OPEN BY EIGHT STROKES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN WINS AUSTRALIAN OPEN BY EIGHT STROKES.

text.p: World number one Greg Norman won the Australian Open by eight strokes on Sunday, firing a final round of three-under-par 69 to outclass a field which included rising U.S. star Tiger Woods.
Australia's Norman finished on eight-under 280, well clear of compatriot Wayne Grady at the Australian Golf Club course.
Norman led by four shots overnight and was the only player to finish under par after heavy rain and high winds over the first three days saw the rest of the field struggle.

Woods, whose 79 on Thursday was his worst round as a professional, finished on four-over 292 after a final round of 70 for equal fifth with Irishman Paul McGinley, New Zealand's Grant Waite and Peter O'Malley of Australia.

The 20-year-old American, playing in his first tournament outside the United States, had said he hoped he could catch Norman despite being 11 shots behind. That faint hope disappeared when Woods bogeyed the par-three second hole.

Norman, the defending champion who has now won five Australian Open titles in 20 starts, told reporters the win was encouraging as he makes minor changes to his swing after linking with new coach David Leadbetter last month.
"It's very encouraging and a big confidence boost that I can change coaches and get a result very quickly," Norman said.
"That's the important thing for my head right now."
Woods picked up a cold during Friday's rain-affected second round but admitted his first round 79 had made his task of challenging the leaders almost impossible.
"My sickness had a little bit to do with not playing well but, then again, it had a lot to do with the fact I didn't hit the ball as sharp as I should have on the first day," he said.
"When you shoot a number like (79) it's very hard to come back. I got it around and finished four over, which is respectable, but I should have done a lot better," he said.
Grady had started eight shots behind Norman in sixth place but finished with a 69 to leap-frog four players, including Sweden's Klas Eriksson who had been second overnight.

Eriksson, who said on Saturday he had been overawed playing next to Norman, closed with his second successive 76 to drop back to fourth on 291. New Zealand's David Smail finished with a 73 to take third on 290.
